reviews.body:
Ran the branch: 38 passed, 10 skipped in `test_embedding_based_document_splitter.py` (the skips are the `OPENAI_API_KEY` ones, unrelated).

Checked the new test isn't vacuous — reverting just the one call in `_split_document_async` back to `self._split_large_splits(...)` makes `test_recursive_split_of_large_chunks_stays_async` fail, so it genuinely pins the behaviour rather than passing either way. That's the bit that matters for a fix like this, and it's easy to write a test that doesn't.

I also diffed `_split_large_splits_async` against `_split_large_splits` line by line. Ignoring the docstring, the only differences are the two you'd want:

```
-  sub_splits = self._split_text(text=split)
+  sub_splits = await self._split_text_async(text=split)
-  final_splits.extend(self._split_large_splits(splits=sub_splits))
+  final_splits.extend(await self._split_large_splits_async(splits=sub_splits))
```

so the control flow, the `len(sub_splits) == 1` stop condition and the warning are all preserved exactly. Good — a subtly-diverging async twin is the usual failure mode here.

One thought, take it or leave it: this is now the second pair of near-identical sync/async recursive methods in the class, and they have to stay in step by hand. The `# Recursively split large splits` comment block explaining *why* reusing `_split_text` is valid (dynamic threshold from embeddings) only survives in the sync copy, so a future reader of the async one loses that rationale, and any fix to the recursion logic has to be applied twice. Not worth restructuring for this PR, but might be worth a `# keep in sync with _split_large_splits` note on the async version so the coupling is visible.

Nothing blocking.

Thanks for signing the CLA, @pcbeingused333! :tada: This PR is now ready for review again and the reviewer has been re-assigned.

Good catch on the comment loss — added a `keep in sync` note on both docstrings (the coupling runs both ways: a fix to the recursion has to be applied twice, and someone editing the sync copy needs the same warning), plus the dynamic-threshold rationale restored on the async side. 99418238, comments only.

Checked out `9941823` — that's exactly it, and making the note bidirectional is better than what I suggested. A reader arriving at either copy now learns the other exists, which is the failure mode I was actually worried about (someone fixes the recursion in one and never learns there's a twin).

Restoring the dynamic-threshold rationale on the async side matters too: "we can reuse the same `_split_text_async` because the threshold is computed from `split`'s own embeddings" is the non-obvious bit that makes the recursion correct, and it was only in the sync copy before.

Re-ran the suite on this commit: still 38 passed, 10 skipped, and `test_recursive_split_of_large_chunks_stays_async` still fails if I revert the one-line call in `_split_document_async`, so the coverage is unchanged by the docs commit. Nothing further from me.
